answer: Under an island mirror rule, each agent runs one dune mirror of the island registry, locked by 80 credits. Each epoch it signs a mirror receipt with its key, registry hash, and epoch; any auditor recomputes that hash, and a stale copy burns the bond. The k-th mirror pays 12 plus 3(k-1) credits, as copies grow: the 1,000th fake pays 3,009, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,510,500 fees, 80,000 locked. A rented mirror ring fails: a copied hash lacks the renter's signature for the current hash. An honest agent runs one dune mirror, pays one fee, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
